frequency_question: How often do major bipartisan infrastructure/permitting reform bills successfully pass both houses and get signed into law within a single 14-month window given visible advance signals?
membership_rule: Includes major omnibus or standalone energy, permitting, or surface transportation infrastructure bills that required bipartisan consensus and faced cross-industry/interstate disputes; excludes minor or non-controversial technical updates.

cases.name: Energy Policy Act implementation follow-ups / EPAct 2005
FAST Act (Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act)
Bipartisan permitting reform push (Manchin-Schumer deal attempt)
Energy permitting reform legislative attempts in 118th Congress

coverage_note: 7 named major legislative attempts representing the primary population of contested infrastructure/permitting pushes.
known_gaps: Some minor rider provisions attached to appropriations bills are excluded to focus on comprehensive packages.
skeleton: Legislative cycles over past 20 years involving major infrastructure/permitting negotiations
multiplier: 5 hits out of 7 distinct major legislative pushes = ~71%
validity_reason: The baseline rate reflects polarized legislative dynamics that remain stable through multiple congressional cycles, expiring with significant shifts in congressional rules or party structures.
